question: Can a required case take the ActiveMQ broker away and prove that the bus reconnects to it, without the test process ever touching a container?
answerToday: No, and the obstacle is the fixture rather than the transport. Three mechanisms were measured and each fails for its own reason. Every remaining option changes the pinned fixture, which is a decision for the Lead.

establishedFacts.fact: compose stop followed by compose start rebinds the published port.
establishedFacts.measurement: OpenWire 127.0.0.1:32955 before, 127.0.0.1:32958 after; AMQP 32953 before, 32956 after.
establishedFacts.consequence: A bus configured with the first address cannot reconnect to the broker: the address it holds is not where the broker came back. A case built on this measures the fixture, not recovery.

establishedFacts.fact: docker pause keeps the published port.
establishedFacts.measurement: 127.0.0.1:32961 before, during and after the pause.
establishedFacts.consequence: The endpoint survives, so this is the only mechanism where reconnecting to the configured address is even meaningful.

establishedFacts.fact: A paused container is not observable as an unreachable port through the port forwarder.
establishedFacts.measurement: The runner's TCP connect to the published port still succeeded after pause, for the full 60 s confirmation budget: 'the broker port still accepts connections after interrupt'. The host side forwarder completes the handshake while the container's processes are frozen.
establishedFacts.consequence: The runner cannot confirm the outage it was asked for, and an unconfirmed outage is refused rather than assumed.

establishedFacts.fact: docker network disconnect drops the port mapping.
establishedFacts.measurement: Port present before, absent while disconnected, and 32961 became 32964 after reconnecting.
establishedFacts.consequence: Same defect as stop and start.

establishedFacts.fact: A publish issued while the broker is frozen does not return - not the task, the call.
establishedFacts.measurement: Three category runs hung until a watchdog killed them; the focused run located it in the publish that resolves a send endpoint against a session whose broker is not answering.
establishedFacts.consequence: A case may not act on the bus during this kind of outage. It also means a frozen broker is not the failure mode the transport recovers from: there is nothing to notice, because nothing was refused.

alsoLearned.finding: A case that leaves the broker paused turns one red case into a run that never ends, because every later fixture of the category blocks against it.
alsoLearned.correction: The runner undoes an outage unconditionally in its teardown, and the helper's restore takes no cancellation token so it still runs after a case has failed or timed out.

whatWasBuiltAndKept: tools/ci/run_broker_category.py --allow-broker-outage: the runner alone touches Docker, answers only what it has observed, refuses a request whose effect it cannot confirm, and undoes any outage in its teardown.
tools/ci/run_broker_category.py --command: a deliberately started scenario runs inside the same fixture boundary as a category.
tests/.../FixtureOutage.cs: the test side of that boundary.

optionsForTheLead.option: A stable TCP proxy in front of the broker
optionsForTheLead.how: The fixture publishes the proxy's ephemeral port; the proxy reaches the broker by service name on the internal network. Restarting the broker leaves the published address untouched, and the outage is genuine: connections are refused and existing ones are closed.
optionsForTheLead.pro: It is the only option that produces a real broker restart behind a stable address, which is what the directive asks for. It also gives fault injection for the other transports later.
optionsForTheLead.contra: It adds a container image to the pinned fixture, which is a change to the frozen dependency contract and to images.lock.json.

optionsForTheLead.option: A fixed host port for the broker used by the outage case
optionsForTheLead.how: Publish 61616 and 5672 on fixed host ports for that one fixture, so stop and start return the broker to the same address.
optionsForTheLead.pro: No new image and no new dependency.
optionsForTheLead.contra: It gives up the ephemeral port rule the directive named as good and to be kept, and it collides with any broker already running on the developer machine, which is exactly what the ephemeral ports were introduced to avoid.

optionsForTheLead.option: Leave the capability uncovered and say so
optionsForTheLead.how: The fixture comment and this record state that recovery from a broker that goes away is not covered, and no test claims it.
optionsForTheLead.pro: Nothing is claimed that is not proven, and no fixture changes.
optionsForTheLead.contra: A real capability of the product stays unverified.

recommendation.option: A stable TCP proxy in front of the broker
recommendation.why: It is the only one that answers the directive as written - a real disconnect, restart and reconnect for both protocol variants - and it keeps every property of the fixture the directive asked to preserve, including ephemeral publishing and the rule that the test process never touches a container. The cost is one pinned image, which is exactly the kind of decision section 7 says to ask about before the edit rather than to make on the way.
